problem_type: Two generation engines answer the same provider fact (an explicit, on-the-spot rejection) with different money semantics
symptom: The canvas engine records a provider rejection (HTTP 4xx such as content policy, invalid parameters or insufficient balance) as a plain failure the user can retry, while the production Run outbox records the same answer as submission_unknown and locks the shot until manual reconciliation; merging the canvas into the Run would lock a canvas node on every moderation refusal
direct_cause: submissionOutbox.submitOnce only distinguished 'provably never written' from 'anything else'; every failure after a byte was written became submission_unknown, including a response in which the provider explicitly refused the task and returned no task id
class_root: No single owner answered 'did the provider accept this submission?' for the case where a response was received; executors threw the provider's answer away as a generic error, so the outbox could not tell a refusal from a lost receipt
affected_population: Canvas single-node generations once they converge onto the production Run (engine convergence cut 1)
Agent / MCP / batch production shots whose provider returned 4xx or a failed 2xx envelope
entry_points: Engine A paid submission through vendorHttp.requestVendor (canvas transport, wrapped by the canvas Run in cut 1)
Engine B paid submission through the catalog generation provider send()
Production submission outbox for every Run-owned job (single shot, multi shot, rework)

external_sources.purpose: 4xx means the server did not process the request because of a client error; 5xx means the server failed and may have partially processed it

invariants: Only a received response with status 4xx, or 2xx carrying a failed envelope, and no task id, counts as an explicit rejection
An explicit rejection settles the job as needs_attention/provider_rejected with a provider-safe reservation release; it is never submission_unknown
5xx, no response, or a partially read response remain submission_unknown and are never auto-resent

door_reduction.why_not: Executors only record the received answer (four providerAnswer readers: two executors, the error class, the judge); the submission seam and the outbox both ask the single judge providerExplicitlyRejected; the 'not charged' predicate jobEndedBeforeAcceptance is the one reader-facing summary used by the presentation and jobMayHaveReachedProvider. No door classifies provider errors on its own.

generality_proof: Both executors attach the provider's answer only after a response is received, and every Run-owned submission passes through submissionOutbox, which asks the one judge in outboundDispatchEvidence.ts; no caller classifies provider errors itself.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Single judge of whether a received provider answer proves the submission was refused and not accepted.
Durably settles an explicitly rejected job as not charged.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The response-failure throw attaches providerAnswer; network, timeout and redirect throws do not (providerExplicitRejection.test.ts loopback cases).
Both the non-JSON response and the rejected-envelope throws attach providerAnswer; fetch failures keep only their cause chain (providerExplicitRejection.test.ts engine B cases).
Custom call scripts build their own VendorRequestError without a received-response answer, so they stay conservatively unknown; they are not Run-owned until the canvas transport is wrapped.

recurrence.reason: Every provider refusal on every Run-owned path hits the same outbox branch; with the canvas converging onto the Run it would happen on the most used surface.

prevention.invariant: A job is settled as not charged only on proof: never written, or a received explicit refusal without a task id.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing or malformed evidence is treated as submission_unknown.
prevention.strategy: Executors record facts (status, envelope, task id) on the error; the single judge decides; the outbox writes the durable outcome.

legacy_paths.rationale: The catch-all that turned an explicit refusal into submission_unknown is replaced in the same change; no fallback classification remains.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The invariant is application-level money semantics over HTTP status codes; no third-party runtime decides it.

migration: Existing submission_unknown jobs are not rewritten; they stay in manual reconciliation. Only new submissions use the third class.
residual_risks: A gateway that returns 4xx after creating an upstream task would now be treated as not charged; accepted by the user on 2026-10-05 (F3).
Custom-call scripts and synchronous audio runners do not attach the answer yet and remain conservatively unknown.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The single judge reads the executor-attached answer; the outbox persists the outcome.
